chunks: Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from al-'Is ibn al-Qasim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a group of people who accepted Islam during the Month of Ramadan after some days of it had already passed: are they required to fast what has passed of it, or their day on which they accepted Islam? He said: "There is no qada' upon them, nor [must they fast] their day on which they accepted Islam, unless they had accepted Islam on it before the rising of dawn."

key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the Month of Ramadan, the obligatory month of sawm
key_terms.طُلُوعِ الْفَجْرِ: the rise of dawn, the legal beginning time of the fasting day
key_terms.قَضَاءٌ: make-up fasting owed for missed obligatory fasts
key_terms.يَصُومُوا: to fast in the legal sense of sawm

ai.seo_question: If someone converts to Islam during Ramadan, must they fast previous days or the same day?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning those who embrace Islam during Ramadan after part of the month has already passed. Imam Abu Abdullah عليه السلام states that they do not owe qada' for earlier days, nor must they fast the day they enter Islam, unless their acceptance of Islam occurred before fajr.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1931 - Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Al-'Is ibn al-Qasim, who said:

"I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a group of people who converted to Islam during the Month of Ramadan after some days had passed. Are they required to fast the days that have passed, or the day they embraced Islam?
Imam (as) said: 'They are not required to make up the missed days or to fast on the day they embraced Islam, unless they embraced Islam before the break of dawn on that day.'"
